rites.name: Grimurnoth
rites.text: Grimurnoth is the concept of the low, patient hum that ran through Thurkok during the Singing, when the first roots of the world condensed out of silence. It has no mind of its own and is known only through the stones and sap it left behind as they took shape.

rites.name: Kathugar
rites.text: Kathugar is the concept of a resonant hum that settled through the first roots of Thurkok during the Singing, when the world's bedrock first condensed out of sound. In the Age of Strangers it became the bond outsiders used to anchor their trade-ships to the shifting ground.

rites.name: Seitheth
rites.text: Seitheth is the concept of threshold-keeping in Thurkok, the principle by which a door is held shut or opened in the Courts. It is invoked during councils to decide which passages between worlds remain sealed.

rites.name: Anamarira
rites.text: Anamarira is a concept of Thurkok, the principle that a wall is only as strong as the oath kept beside it, born in the Walled Age when the first orders learned to hold a city against the dark. Its teachings spread through the flame-lit temples of the Holy Age, where believers carried it across the first crossings between settlements.
